label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: The chief task at the week-end has been to keep open the docks—a process which began on Friday with the removal of, inter alia, over 100 lorry loads of flour and 700 tons of sugar, the task being successfully pursued.

label: paragraph_title
text: More Direct Action.

label: text
text: The latest reports show an intensification of the tendency for more direct action by the strikers, especially against food and particularly flour mills, but no appreciable effect is at present felt except in isolated districts like Smithfield and parts of the dock area.

label: text
text: Paper Supplies.

label: text
text:
Another Armed Convoy.
Yesterday's armed convoy of flour was repeated to-day, when 150 lorries with armed soldiers sitting on the flour sacks, flanked by armoured cars with a squadron of cavalry in the rear passed through the inflammable dock area peacefully, and dumped the cargo in Hyde Park.

label: text
text: In Newcastle the police were hurriedly reinforced last night to deal with a disorderly crowd of 10,000 who were attacking the special constables.

label: text
text: The crowd was broken up, in sections and dispersed with the aid of batons.

text: Attempt at Rescue.

label: paragraph_title
text: "UNCHANGED."

label: paragraph_title
text: Overcoming Obstruction by Pickets

label: text
text: An official communique says that the general situation is unchanged.

label: text
text:
Obstruction by the pickets is being more effectually overcome.
There is complete confidence that order will be maintained in the London dock area, where the loading and unloading of vessels by volunteers are proceeding and increasing. It is intended to keep the Port of London regularly opened. The situation in Scotland has also improved. The food and fuel position everywhere is satisfactory.

label: text
text: London, May 9..

label: text
text: His Majesty the King held a Council at Buckingham Palace, the Earl of Balfour, the Attorney-general and the Home Secretary being present.

label: paragraph_title
text: NO ENTHUSIASM.

label: paragraph_title
text: Cold Water On Delegate's Proposal.

label: text
text: Ostend, May 9

label: text
text: The transport workers at the international Labour Conference did not enthuse over the proposal of the British delegate, Mr. Milford, that the loading and unloading of every ship flying the British flag should be prohibited at all Continental ports whatever her cargo.

label: text
text: The Belgian delegate pointed out the impossibility of complying with this proposal, especially in connection with the unloading of cargoes destined for local consumption.

label: text
text: Eventually it was agreed that coal consignments for Great Britain would be prevented at all continental ports.

label: text
text: The International Miners' Committee announced their solidarity with the British workers, declaring their readiness to take still further steps to assist them, and expressing the conviction that lasting peace in the mining industry is only possible through the establishment of co-operation with International control.

label: paragraph_title
text: DIFFERENT REVOLUTION

label: paragraph_title
text: Earl Balfour's Plain Warning.

label: text
text: Earl Balfour, in an article in the "British Gazette," says that 238 years have passed since a revolution in this country, the object of which was to secure the supremacy of Parliamentary Government and the traditional liberties of our people but we are now threatened with a very different kind of revolution, the methods of which consist of depriving the people of food transport, employment and a free

label: text
text: "He points out that no revolution in Great Britain, however triumphant, is going to diminish competition in neutral markets, augment the demand for coal at Home, hasten the changes recommended by the Coal Commission, or compel the mine owner indefinitely to carry on his industry at a loss." Revolutionary methods would be completely powerless except for evil."

label: text
text: Earl Balfour declares that if the revolution were to succeed the community thenceforth would be ruled by a relatively small body of extremists, who regard the Trade Unions not as machinery for collective bargaining within our industrial system, but as a political instrument by means of which our industrial system may be utterly destroyed. He says that such a policy must eventually be fatal to any country. On Great Britain it would bring ruin, swift

label: text
text: "We live on industry." Industry lives on credit and enterprise. What credit, financial and political, what enterprise would remain to us were we driven by such methods to dispossess the people of their Parliamentary liberties and hand over our national heritage to be squandered amid incalculable suffering by violent and irresponsible doctrinaires? From such fate may the courage and resolution of our countrymen save civilisation, of which they are trustees."

label: paragraph_title
text: EARLIER NEWS.

label: text
text: London, May 8

label: text
text: It is officially stated that the situation all over the country is satisfactory. There are ample supplies of foodstuffs in practically every district. The country is quiet. There were no disturbances in the last 24 hours, except a few minor incidents.

label: text
text: The Government appeals for recruits for the "Civil Constabulary Reserve," who will be paid as a whole-time force: Special, constables are being organised into units, weaning plain clothes, and are supplied with armlets, steel helmets and truncheons, and are formed from ex-Service men, the ago limit being fifty, and Territorials and Training Corps officers.

label: text
text: Three hundred and five passengers landed at Southampton by the 2.8. "Leviathan," and proceeded to London in charabancé. 2,800 bags of mail were also despatched.

label: text
text: Pickets of the Portsmouth Corporation Electricity Works who endvoured to persuade men not to go in, have them themselves now been finally cajoled to work.

label: text
text: Amsterdam, May 8

label: text
text: The Netherlands Trade Unions Congress has voted £5,000 for the British strikers, payable in three weekly instalments.

label: text
text: A joint sitting of the International Socialist and Labour Bureau Committee and the International Federation of Trades. Unions will be held at Amsterdam on Tuesday to discuss the international situation in relation to the strike in Britain.

label: text
text: London, May 8.

label: text
text: The “British Worker” states the Council of the Trades Union Congress have declined the offer of aid from the Russian Trade Union, and have returned their cheque. At a meeting of the Miners' Executive Mr. Cook declared there was no change, and no sign of any peace moves.

label: text
text:
Towards the close of the debate on Emergency Regulations in the House of Commons on Thursday evening. Sir John Simon made a speech which led to a lively discussion in political Labour circles as regards the future of Trade Unionism. Sir John while not denying the workman's right to strike said the present general strike, which disregarded all contracts of employment, was not a lawful act and from this viewpoint the future of Trade Unionism was in a tragic situation. Labour leaders were abusing the power given to them by the Trade Dispute Act, and unless they were careful there might be a terrible reaction.

Numerous factories are beginning to feel the lack of raw materials.

A destroyer was sent to Manchester where two food ships were unloaded by patrol naval motorboats.

label: text
text:
Three hundred combine embibuses are running in London, and Welsh and Yorkshire newspapers are selling in London.
The Trade Unions' Council have informed Trade Unions that shipments from Ireland to Britain should cease. Isolated holganism is proceeding. The Miners' conduct is exemplary, the transport men only being troublesome.

label: text
text: Mr. Brown, the prominent Communist of Doncaster, who recently returned from Moscow was sentenced to three years' imprisonment for a seditious speech. The Financial Secretary to the

label: text
text: Efforts were made yesterday to rush the London, Midland and Scottish Railway office at Crewe, owing to the railway refusing to pay strikers' wages. The Police dispersed the crowd. No damage was done.

label: text
text: Sir John Simon's speech in the Commons at the close of the debate on Thursday night has received much attention in political and Labour circles in view of Sir John's position as a legal authority and his past championship of Trade Unionism.

label: text
text: The Cardiff "Western Mall" (one of the prominent provincial papers whose eight-page production is widely circulated in London) in a editorial says as the result of the speech "Trade Union officials concerned in the general strike must understand they are liable any moment to be sued in the Courts by persons they have wronged and whose trade they are seeking to injure. Probably 75 per cent. of the strikers struck unwillingly," and these are now assured by Sir John Simon that the protection of the law will be accorded to them if they have courage enough to disobey the unlawful and tyrannous orders of the Trade Union officials, and re

label: text
text: Sir John Simon's speech evoked a reply from the "British Worker," the official strike news bulletin, which in a manifesto headed "Misleading the Nation" declares "There is no attack on the community, no attempt to set up a rival government," no challenge to "the Constitution." The workers have exercised their legal and long-established right to withhold their labour in order to protect the miners against the degradation of their standard life, which is a menace to the whole world of Labour. If in exercise of that right contracts have been broken, that incident as Sir John Simon must well be aware, cannot with any show of reason be used to give the present struggle the sinister character which he has chosen to ascribe to it.

label: text
text: The manifesto after emphasising the origin and object of the struggle as purely industrial, says the struggle will continue until the Government are willing to resume negotiations for an honourable termination of the mining dispute.

label: text
text: The Trade Union Congress states that reports from the greater part of the country to-day show that solidarity is being maintained and men are still coming out in "Our second line of defence." The T.U.C. is of the opinion that "the argument of Sir John Simon and the Cabinet that the T.U.C. are attempting to overthrow the Constitution and undermine Parliamentary institutions is a willful and deliberate attempt to confuse the issue and prejudice the position of the Trade Union movement by the allegation that we have received money from Moscow. This morning a cheque arrived from the Alli-Russian Central Council of Trade Unions, Moscow, running to some thousands. We fully considered the matter, and decided to send a courteous reply expressing appreciation, but inability to accept the cheque which was returned."

label: text
text: The T.U.C. points out the Secretary of the Free Church Council has refuted a statement that the organisation has placed itself at the disposal of the Government.

label: text
text: It also says the London pickets report that 90 per cent. of the goods coming to London are coming by road, and not rail. The T.U.C. has decided to instruct the Unions that all men working are liable to 5 per cent. of their wages as Strike Levy. The Council is appealing to the Trade Unions and sympathisers abroad for financial help.

label: text
text: Britain, France, Germany, Belgium, Holland, Spain, Luxembourg and Czechoslovakia were represented at a meeting of the International Miners' Committee. The British representatives, Messrs. Richardson and Frank Hodges, arrived by aeroplane, and explained the situation in Britain.

label: text
text: It was announced that the decision of the recent Brussels conference that no coal be exported to Britain had been fully carried out by either country.

label: text
text:
Berne, May 9.
At a meeting at Olten the Committee of the Swise Union of Syndicates decided to appeal to Swiss workers to support the strike in Britain. The Unions have undertaken to contribute at least a franc for each of their members for the British strikers.
Donald, May 9.

label: text
text: The "British Gazette" officially notifies all workers that every man doing his duty by the country in the present crisis will be protected by the State from reprisals and loss of benefits or pension, and that legislation for that purpose will be

label: text
text: A return to normal shipping conditions is gradually being made both at Liverpool and Southampton, says the "British Gazette."

label: text
text: The position at Liverpool has improved to such an extent that eighteen vessels were docked and ten others undocked on Thursday. Volunteer labour continues to pour in.

label: text
text: Sixteen vessels were discharging on Friday by three thousand men. Many of the dock strikers have reported for duty.

label: text
text: Ship's crews are continuing to sign on in large numbers.

label: text
text: A sufficient supply of volunteer labour is available at Southampton.

label: text
text: The Norddeutscher Lloyd liner Columbus and the Cunard liner Ascania sailed according to schedule.

label: text

Many ships are discharging
cargo

label: text
text: The Southern Railways cross-Channel boats are running as arranged.

label: text
text: The Union Castler liner Kildonan Castle is fully bunkered and stored, ready to sail.

label: text
text: The Berwick-Newcastle train was attacked last night.

label: text
text: The driver noticed the level crossing gate foul of the line and slowed up.

label: text
text: Suddenly, a mob of 300 or 400 men appeared on both sides of the line and bombarded the train with heavy stones.

label: text
text: A big stone smashed the glass of the driver's cabin, grazed the driver's neck, and hit the stoker.

label: text
text: Regent's Park has been closed to the public, and the Police are guarding the entrances. Paris, May 7.

label: text
text: The Press comments on the general strike in Great Britain emphasise its political aspect as a step toward social revolution. They are of opinion that Great Britain's resistance to it will be victorious.

label: text
text: $ ^{0} $ The Communist newspaper Humanite publishes a manifesto from the General Confederation of Labour announcing its decision to open a national subscription list in support of the British strikers.

label: text
text: “The issue now is not what wages the miners should be given but whether democratic Parliamentary Government is to be overthrown,” says Viscount Grey in a message to the “British Gazette” in which he points out that the alternatives are Fascism or Communism which are both hostile and fatal to liberty.

label: text
text: Mannwhile, he states, every day of the strike is making the future worse for everybody. "Two things are clear—first that the community must work together at all costs to avert a revolution and to preserve constitutional method and the second that the only counsel to save our industries and end the strike is to get back to negotiations."

label: text
text: Further disturbances occurred in Glasgow last night. Forty-eight arrests had been made up to midnight.

label: text
text: Pickets stopped petrol lorries at East Stanfordlehope. Three arrest were made as the result.

label: text
text: A number of telegraph wires between Newcastle and Hexham were cut.

label: text
text: The city of London to-day was almost like Sunday. Many of the offices and shops closed in order to give a rest to their employees, many of whom had to walk long distances.

label: text
text: The strikers at the Yarmouth Corporation Electricity Power Station have resumed work.

label: text
text: There was a collision between Royalists and Police to-day, when several Policemen and demonstrators were injured.

label: text
text:
Twenty arrests were made.
The occasion of the celebration
was the fete day of Jeanne d'Arc.

label: text

label: text
text: Thirty-one, persons, have been taken into custody.

label: text
text: INCIDENT AT CONNAUGHT ROAD WEST.

label: paragraph_title
text: ANOTHER ARREST.

label: text
text: A Chinese arrested by a detective after a chase in the water on Saturday afternoon was brought before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning and formally charged with participation in an armed robbery at No. 35, Connaught Road West.

label: text
text:
This makes the third arrest in connection with this robbery, one of the alleged robbers being in hospital with a bullet wound in the neck while an employee of the shop is also in police custody.
One week's formal remand was granted in the present case when Det. Sub-Inspector Lane mentioned that the wounded man's condition was reported to be dangerous.

label: text
text: A traveller stopping near a small shack by the roadside in Kentucky said to the woman who came to the door:

label: text
text:
"Where is your husband?"
"Down yonder in the field," the woman replied.

label: text
text: "Which one of those two men is your husband?"

label: text
text: "They's only one man down yonder. T'other one is a scarecrow."

label: text
text: "All right, I'll go down there and see him."

label: text
text: "Look and see which one moves the most, and t'other one will be Hank.
